name: Rosetta Stone
tagline: Build a picture-and-audio practice sequence from user-owned material

pricing.notes: Typical monthly subscription; promotions and lifetime offers are common.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Rosetta Stone, build a picture-and-audio practice sequence from user-owned material. The hard boundary is licensed curriculum, speech engine, tutoring, mobile apps, and long-running pedagogy, plus content, pedagogy, and network.
coreLoopDIY: Build a picture-and-audio practice sequence from user-owned material, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
requirements: optional speech or language-model API key
whatYouLose: licensed curriculum, speech engine, tutoring, mobile apps, and long-running pedagogy
ongoingBurden: curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Rosetta Stone because the learning loop is buildable, while trusted curriculum, instructors, feedback, credentials, and community are not. The recurring cost buys curriculum quality, assessment validity, content rights, spaced-repetition tuning, speech models, sync, moderation, and support, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Single language plan and a personal study companion DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Rosetta Stone in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and a service worker for offline use; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a picture-and-audio practice sequence from user-owned material, schedule retrieval practice, and show progress without claiming accredited instruction.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Import Markdown, text, or user-authored notes and split them into editable learning units.
Create flashcards and short quizzes only after showing the generated items for approval.
Implement a transparent spaced-repetition schedule with due, again, hard, good, and easy actions.
Add goals, study sessions, streak-free progress charts, notes, and weak-topic review.
For language practice, record the learner and compare timing or pronunciation without presenting medical claims.
Support offline use, full export, reset, backup, and deletion of all learning data.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out licensed premium courses.
Deliberately leave out accredited certificates and grading.
Deliberately leave out live tutors, large classrooms, and a learner marketplace.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
